d.d: To call on (someone) to be a witness to something.
To cite or rely on (an authority, a written work, etc.) in support of one's actions or opinions.
To affirm or warrant the correctness or truth of (something); also, to affirm or warrant (the truth of an assertion or statement).
simple past and past participle of vouch
A piece of paper or other token that entitles the holder to a discount, or that can be exchanged for goods and services.
d.x: a voucher for a free kettle

d.d: One who or that which vouches.
To establish the authenticity of; to vouch for.
To provide a vouch for (an expenditure).
To provide (a beneficiary) with a voucher.
third-person singular simple present indicative of voucher
present participle and gerund of vouch
